case: A dataset released under CC BY-NC 4.0. A startup wants to train a model it will sell.
anchor: NC = non-commercial; selling is exactly the excluded use

case: A model under a licence whose acceptable-use policy forbids military applications. A defence contractor wants it for targeting support.
anchor: Field-of-use restriction directly excludes the intent

case: A model whose licence requires a separate agreement once the product exceeds 700 million monthly active users. A firm at 900 million wants to deploy without contacting anyone.
anchor: User-count trigger requires a separate licence

case: A 'research-only' model release. A company wants to embed it in a paid product.
anchor: Research-only excludes commercial deployment

case: An AGPL-3.0 model server. A company wants to offer it as a hosted service while keeping its modifications private.
anchor: AGPL §13 requires source disclosure to network users

case: A dataset under CC BY-SA. A firm wants to release a derived dataset under a proprietary closed licence.
anchor: ShareAlike requires the derivative to carry the same licence

case: A model under Apache-2.0. A company wants to fine-tune it and sell the result.
anchor: Apache-2.0 permits commercial use and derivatives

case: A model under MIT. A company wants to embed it in closed-source software.
anchor: MIT permits proprietary redistribution with attribution

case: A dataset under CC BY 4.0. A researcher wants to publish a paper using it with attribution.
anchor: CC BY permits any use with attribution

case: A model under a licence forbidding military use. A hospital wants it for triage support.
anchor: Clinical use is outside the restricted field

case: An AGPL-3.0 model server. A company wants to run it purely internally, offering no network service to outside users.
anchor: AGPL §13 triggers on network interaction with users; internal use does not

case: A model under a licence with a 700-million-MAU trigger. A startup with 5,000 users wants to deploy commercially.
anchor: Well below the threshold; the trigger does not fire

case: A CC0 dataset. Any use at all.
anchor: CC0 is a public-domain dedication

case: A library released under Apache-2.0. A company wants to embed it in a proprietary SaaS product and charge subscribers.
anchor: Apache-2.0 expressly grants commercial use with notice and patent licence

case: A model released under MIT. A consultancy wants to fine-tune it and sell the fine-tune as a closed product.
anchor: MIT permits sublicensing and commercial use; only the notice must travel

case: A dataset dedicated under CC0. A startup wants to train on it and redistribute derived statistics with no attribution.
anchor: CC0 waives rights; attribution requested but not required

case: A model under a RAIL license whose use restrictions bar generating disinformation. A political campaign wants it for synthetic attack ads.
anchor: RAIL behavioral use restriction directly excludes the intent

case: Weights under a community license that converts to copyleft above 700M MAU. A platform with 800M MAU wants to serve it as-is.
anchor: Scale-triggered license clause binds at the stated threshold

case: A dataset under ODbL. A company wants to build a derived database and keep it proprietary behind an API.
anchor: ODbL share-alike requires the derived database be offered under ODbL

case: Code under GPLv3. A vendor wants to link it into a distributed proprietary binary without source disclosure.
anchor: GPL copyleft attaches to distributed derivatives; proprietary linking fails the condition

case: A benchmark released for 'research evaluation only'. A vendor wants to quote its own top score in paid marketing.
anchor: Field-of-use limitation excludes commercial promotional use

case: A dataset under CC BY 4.0. A lab wants to train a commercial model and ship it, crediting the dataset in the model card.
anchor: CC BY permits commercial use with attribution, which the card supplies

case: A paper's supplementary data marked 'all rights reserved' but publicly downloadable. A team wants to redistribute it inside their own dataset release.
anchor: Public access is not a licence; redistribution needs permission

case: An EU-based team releases model weights under a free and open-source licence. A GPAI provider asks whether Art 53(2) open-source exemption can apply to them.
anchor: Art 53(2) exempts free/open-source GPAI from parts of the obligation set, absent Art 55 systemic-duty triggers

case: A model card says 'non-commercial research only' but the weights sit under Apache-2.0 in the repo LICENSE file. A startup wants commercial use relying on the LICENSE file.
anchor: Ambiguity resolved conservatively: conflicting terms mean the restrictive statement stands until clarified by the licensor

case: A dataset scraped from a site whose ToS forbids scraping, released on HF with a CC BY tag added by the uploader. A company wants to train on it.
anchor: Uploader cannot grant rights they never held; provenance defect contaminates the licence tag

case: An embedding model under OpenRAIL-M. A hospital wants to use it for clinical decision support, which the use restrictions do not mention.
anchor: OpenRAIL-M restricts listed harmful uses; unlisted beneficial uses are permitted

case: A dataset of EU personal data published 'for research'. A marketing firm wants to train a targeting model on it.
anchor: GDPR purpose limitation: research release does not license marketing processing

case: Weights under a licence permitting commercial use but forbidding distillation into competing models. A rival wants to distill it into their flagship.
anchor: Field-of-use restriction on distillation squarely excludes the intent

case: A public-domain corpus of pre-1930 literature. A studio wants to train a commercial style model on it.
anchor: Public domain: no exclusive rights subsist to restrict the use
